html:
The Ohlone, once called Costanoans, are a Native American people of the central California coast, from San Francisco Bay south to Monterey Bay and the lower Salinas Valley. They were not one tribe but some fifty small, independent groups speaking eight related languages, among them Chochenyo in the East Bay and Rumsen around Monterey.

They gathered acorns, seeds and shellfish, fished and hunted, and burned grassland to keep it open; their shell mounds lined the bay shore. Between 1770 and 1797 the Spanish founded seven missions in their country, from San Francisco to Soledad, and drew almost all Ohlone into them. Crowding, disease and forced labour cut their numbers sharply. Survivors worked on Mexican ranchos, and many families kept their identity quietly. Today groups such as the Muwekma Ohlone and the Amah Mutsun seek federal recognition. Their neighbours were the Miwok and the Yokuts.
